title: Gochujang Five-Spice Belly
why_this: Nothing has been rated yet, so this is a deliberate calibration dish that uses pork belly the way the rack says it wants it: a long marinade and warm spices. Gochujang and soy provide savoury depth with restrained background acidity, while cayenne keeps the heat genuinely present.
pan: Rimmed sheet pan with wire rack - lets the pork render without stewing, then catches the glaze during the final broil.

blend.why: Warm star-anise depth for the fatty pork.
Adds fruity chile flavour and red colour.
Supplies the direct heat that gochugaru lacks.
Adds gentle fruity chile aroma after cooking.
Provides crisp garlic texture without burning it.

salt.when: 6.1g on the bare pork 45 minutes before marinating; 1.0g in the rice; soy and gochujang enter with the marinade.
salt.rationale: Target 9.0g total for 1.5 lb pork plus rice. Add 6.1g salt to the pork + approximately 1.2g salt from 1 tbsp soy sauce + approximately 0.7g from 2 tbsp gochujang + 1.0g in the rice = 9.0g total. No pre-salted rack blend is used.

from_kitchen.amount: 6.1g for the pork; the app should convert this to the shelf salt
1 tsp for the marinade, plus 1 tsp for the rack
1 1/2 cups for the rice, or the amount required by the rice package

steps.title: Dry-brine pork
steps.body: Pat the pork belly dry and rub the bare meat and skin with 6.1g salt. Leave uncovered in the refrigerator for 45 minutes; if convenient, leave it overnight. Do not add any spices yet.
steps.watch_for: The surface should look slightly tacky rather than wet. Pooling liquid means the pork was not patted dry enough.

steps.title: Build marinade
steps.body: Mix Chinese 5 Spice, gochugaru, cayenne, garlic, ginger, gochujang, soy sauce, brown sugar, and 1 tsp oil. Coat the pork thoroughly, cover, and refrigerate for 4 hours. Do not add extra salt.
steps.watch_for: The marinade should be thick and cling to the pork. If it is watery, the coating will slide off and scorch less evenly.

steps.title: Start rice
steps.body: Rinse the rice, combine it with the measured water and 1.0g salt, and cook according to the package directions. Keep covered off heat when done.
steps.watch_for: The grains should be tender with no hard centre. If the rice is wet, leave it covered for 5 minutes longer rather than adding salt.

steps.title: Slow-roast belly
steps.body: Heat the oven to 325°F. Line a rimmed sheet pan, oil the wire rack lightly, and place the pork fat-side up. Scrape off heavy clumps of marinade so they do not blacken, reserving the thin coating on the meat. Roast until deeply browned and fork-tender, about 85-90 minutes.
steps.watch_for: You want steady rendering and dark red-brown edges, not black powdery spots. If the marinade smells acrid or is blackening early, lower the oven to 300°F.

steps.title: Broil the edges
steps.body: Move the rack near the broiler and broil for 2-4 minutes, watching constantly, until the fat blisters and the edges lacquer. Rest the pork for 8 minutes, then slice.
steps.watch_for: The glaze should bubble and turn mahogany. Sugar burns suddenly; pull it as soon as any edge goes from brown to black.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.body: Scatter sesame seeds, Silk Chili (Aleppo), Fried Garlic, and scallions over the sliced pork. Serve immediately with the salted rice and cabbage or garlic chives.
steps.watch_for: The fried garlic should stay crisp and pale golden. If it is dark or bitter, remove it rather than mixing it through the pork.

salt_check: Taste one centre slice with a forkful of rice before serving. It should taste assertively savoury but not briny. If under-seasoned, dissolve 0.3g salt in 1 tsp hot water and brush it over the sliced pork; do not add dry salt directly to the crust.
serve_with: Steamed salted rice, lightly wilted cabbage or garlic chives, and sliced scallions. Keep the vegetable side plain so the pork's garlic, warm spice, and chile remain the focus.
leftovers: Refrigerate pork and rice separately for up to 3 days. Reheat the pork uncovered in a hot oven or air fryer so the fat re-crisps; add the Fried Garlic and Silk Chili only after reheating.
